scope: Round 11 decode attention and selector subsystem. Energy excludes prefill, projections, MLP, sampling and other model work. The first generated token is produced by prefill.
provenance: Illustrative, jointly varied engineering scenarios with uncalibrated coefficients. They describe neither measurement uncertainty nor a specific device or process. The DRAMPower reference supports the structure of the accounting.
dram: One 32 B per RD. RD core counts the core increment, read_io the traffic-dependent interface increment, and background_mw a constant during modeled completion. ACT and PRE reflect the replay command counts. Refresh, writes, WCK behavior, and end-of-group command activity absent from the replay are outside this estimate.
replay_estimator: Ordinary complete replay steps are weighted equally within each exact policy/cohort/lane/PE-period/scorer/mode. Summed ACT, PRE, and descriptor counts divided by sampled RD counts are applied to closed-loop RD counts. Runtime uses mean sampled full-step completion. Selected common-state traces may differ from independently generated states. The byte deltas compare the replay sample to the closed-loop population and to whole-answer means at matched IDs. They describe traffic representativeness. Runtime min/max describe the replay sample.
pressure: Only regular full-step rows enter estimates. True fallbacks found in ordinary closed-loop predictions still enter the workload. Enriched fallback-pressure rows stay in the timing artifact.
compute: Exact scorer terms, fused score updates, and effective QK/PV MAC from closed-loop counters. Product and accumulation costs are separate. Model QK scale and PV weight energy once per effective head-score. KV4 uses one shared affine expansion per fetched physical element and one preparation per scale and zero-point for each 32-channel group. The DRAM byte ledger already includes side-field and alignment bursts.
sram: Modeled logical access bytes. Stage physical read bytes with one write and one read. Charge two-byte unpacked K/V writes, one shared K read per input element, and per-head V reads. Charge four bytes per score write, two histogram score reads, and one PV weight read. Charge histogram initialization and two bin scans plus a read-modify-write per visited candidate score. Protected scores use the same visit accounting. Packed masks use one read and one write, averaged without per-group alignment. Scorer pages and selected IDs use one four-byte write and read per head-score or ID. Count summary append bytes as SRAM writes when logged. This activity does not identify bank utilization or measure SRAM capacity.
control: Histogram/selection work uses candidate head-score visits, all scored pages, and descriptor runs when replayed. Time terms charge baseline and lane clocks throughout completion.
field_availability: Empty cells indicate fields absent from the supplied ledger or replay. Missing descriptor and summary append counters omit those individual contributions. Totals still include control time and SRAM staging.
normalization: Total closed-loop work divided by all generated decode steps for µJ/step. Multiply by actual total decode steps divided by answers for mJ/answer. Every generated answer has one additional token from prefill. ns × mW = pJ.
break_even: Positive delta means the candidate consumes more energy. V coefficient varies combined RD-core and I/O energy per physical V byte. ACT/PRE, SRAM activity, and runtime are held fixed for this coefficient sweep. SRAM coefficient varies energy per modeled access byte. The reported interval spans the lower, nominal and upper settings of remaining coefficients. Crossings can be negative and only nonnegative coefficients are physical. The separate candidate V-byte ceiling varies its physical V bytes, assuming unchanged total ACT/PRE/descriptor intensities, two-byte staging per read byte, and unchanged compute, logical records, and runtime. It tests feasibility only over nonnegative bytes. Actual layouts must preserve protection and whole bursts.
